selected.rationale: The Wellness Optimizer tracks supplements and workouts, aligning directly with the advertiser's functional, science-backed adaptogenic drink, and can be effectively reached on the science-forward Daily Form publisher.

The Gen Z Aesthete has a category affinity for functional beverages and a preference for aesthetic-forward and novelty messaging, making them an ideal match for a trendy sparkling drink and reachable via Pop & Sip.

The Fitness Enthusiast focuses on recovery and functional beverages with low-medium price sensitivity, matching the advertiser's mid-tier adaptogenic beverage aimed at feeling good without a hangover, reachable on Pantrygood and Pop & Sip.

rejected.reason: The Busy Parent prioritizes time-saving meal kits and family products, which does not align with a single-person lifestyle beverage brand or the recommended publishers' audiences.
The Pet Parent focuses on animal health and pet supplies, which is entirely irrelevant to human functional beverages.
The Affluent Classic is aged 50-68 and prefers traditional luxury goods and heritage messaging, missing the younger 21-45 demographic target of the beverage.
The Sustainability Buyer focuses on supply chains and green credentials rather than the functional/wellness benefits emphasized by the advertiser's product.
The Convenience-First Millennial prioritizes instant delivery and general quick commerce subscriptions over a specific functional drink formulation.
The Value-Conscious Shopper has high price sensitivity and looks for budget deals, whereas the advertiser's mid-tier $40 functional beverage requires a less discount-reliant buyer.
The Gifter is focused on seasonal gift sets and impressive presentation, whereas the advertiser sells a routine lifestyle beverage rather than a gift item.
